oi.text: Net interest income is the largest source of the Company’s operating income. For the three and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026, net interest income was $19,802,000 and $57,570,000, respectively, which represents increases of $605,000 and $2,412,000, respectively, from the comparable periods in 2025. The increase was due to growth of earning assets and upward repricing of our loan yield in spite of short-term rate cuts by the FOMC during 2025. The earning asset yield increased by 11 basis points and 7 basis points for the three and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026, respectively, as compared to the same periods of 2025.

prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The Company makes provisions for credit losses when required to bring the total allowance for credit losses to a level deemed appropriate for the level of risk in the loan portfolio. At least quarterly, management conducts an assessment of the overall quality of the loan portfolio and general economic trends in the local market. The determination of the appropriate level for the allowance is based on that review, considering such factors as historical experience, the volume and type of lending conducted, the amount of and identified potential loss associated with specific non-performing loans, regulatory policies, general economic conditions, and other factors, including reasonable and supportable forecasts, related to the collectability of loans in the portfolio.

During the three and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026, the Company recorded provisions for credit losses of $42,000 and $527,000, respectively, consisting of a provision for loan losses of $0 and provisions for off balance sheet items of $42,000 during the third quarter of 2026, and a provision for loan losses of $554,000 and a reversal of provisions for off balance sheet items of $27,000 during the year-to-date period of 2026.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: The Company recorded provisions for income taxes of $1,741,000 and $4,555,000 for the three and nine-months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, representing decreases of $96,000 and $362,000, respectively, compared to the provisions recorded in the comparable periods of 2025. The effective income tax rate on income from continuing operations was 21.3% for the three and nine-months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 21.5% and 21.9%, respectively, for the comparable periods of 2025. These provisions reflect accruals for taxes at the applicable rates for federal income tax and California franchise tax based upon reported pre-tax income, and adjusted for the effects of all permanent differences between income for tax and financial reporting purposes (such as earnings on qualified municipal securities, bank owned life insurance and certain tax-exempt loans). The disparity between the effective tax rates for the year-to-date period of 2026 as compared to 2025 is primarily due to tax credits from low-income housing projects as well as tax-free income on municipal securities and loans that comprised a larger proportion of pre-tax income in 2026 as compared to 2025.

net.text: For the three and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026, the Company recorded net income of $6,450,000 and $16,873,000, respectively, representing decreases of $243,000 and $705,000, respectively, as compared to the same periods in 2025. Return on average assets (annualized) was 1.28% and 1.13% for the three and nine-months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, as compared to 1.35% and 1.22%, respectively, for the same periods in 2025. Annualized return on average common equity was 12.16% and 10.72% for the three and nine-months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, as compared to 14.30% and 12.71%, respectively, for the same periods in 2025. Net income before provisions for income taxes decreased by $339,000 and $1,067,000 for the three and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026, respectively, from the same periods in 2025. Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
Net interest income is the largest source of the Company’s operating income. For the three and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026, net interest income was $19,802,000 and $57,570,000, respectively, which represents increases of $605,000 and $2,412,000, respectively, from the comparable periods in 2025. The increase was due to growth of earning assets and upward repricing of our loan yield in spite of short-term rate cuts by the FOMC during 2025. The earning asset yield increased by 11 basis points and 7 basis points for the three and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026, respectively, as compared to the same periods of 2025.

Due to the current interest rate environment, the Bank has experienced a modest increase in the average interest rate paid on deposit accounts as it continues to competitively price deposits to meet customer demand, maintain deposit relationships, and support liquidity. The Company’s average cost of funds was 0.80% for the three and nine-months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to 0.75% and 0.77%, respectively, in the same periods of 2025.

The net interest margin (net interest income as a percentage of average interest earning assets) was 4.24% and 4.17% for the three and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026, respectively, as compared to 4.16% and 4.12%, respectively, for the same periods in 2025.

intro.text: Oak Valley Bancorp. Oak Valley Bancorp (the “Company”) serves as the parent bank holding company of Oak Valley Community Bank (the “Bank”), a California state-chartered bank. The Bank and the Company may be generally referred to as “we”, “us” or “our”). The Company was incorporated under the laws of the State of California on May 31, 1990, and began operations in Oakdale, California on May 28, 1991. The Company’s only assets are the outstanding capital stock of the Bank, which the Company wholly owns, cash and income tax benefits receivable classified as other assets.

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Equity securities
lines.why: Shares held for their return: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
